subject.title: Validate required run artifacts against a schema (`--require-artifact-schema`)

question: Should Crabbox core own a built-in partial JSON Schema contract for run artifacts, or continue requiring repository commands to validate artifact content?
rationale: Both approaches are technically viable, but choosing one establishes a durable CLI and schema-compatibility boundary that cannot be inferred safely from existing implementation alone.

options.title: Keep Validation Repository-Owned
options.body: Retain the documented existence-only gate and use repository commands or established schema tools to fail the run when evidence is malformed.

options.title: Adopt the Narrow Core Gate
options.body: Approve the proposed bounded, fail-closed schema subset after the linked pull request supplies real SSH-backed integration proof and explicit compatibility documentation.

recommendation.title: Keep Validation Repository-Owned
recommendation.body: Retain the documented existence-only gate and use repository commands or established schema tools to fail the run when evidence is malformed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the required-artifact gate makes this the strongest available routing candidate for its product boundary.
